newsitem.title: UK: UK to inject more competition into water, sewerage.
newsitem.headline: UK to inject more competition into water, sewerage.

text.p: The British government, confirming plans to liberalise water and sewerage services, said it would go farther than originally envisaged and consider allowing competition to supply smaller users.
Environment Secretary John Gummer proposed in a consultation paper last April restricting competition, as at present, to large customers who use more than 250 megalitres of water a year.

But in a written parliamentary answer, he said that as a result of suggestions made during the consultation period the government would consider extending the scope of so-called common carriage and inset appointments to smaller users.
"We will look again to see whether a lower limit, perhaps in the 100-200 megalitre range, would be practicable and appropriate," Gummer said.
Common carriage allows companies to use an existing supplier's network to provide individual customers with a choice of water supply.
Inset arrangements permit a new water or waste water firm to be appointed for part of an existing franchise area.
Gummer said responses to the consultation paper showed broad support for the government's liberalisation proposals.
"In light of the positive response it is our intention to proceed with these proposals with a view to bringing forward legislation in the next parliament," Gummer said.
He said the government would seek to ensure that the quality of water continues to be safeguarded and that the charging regime for water services remains fair and non-discriminatory.
